# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I'm the Blind one. My hands found four things: a display I can't read by touch, a light whose state I can't feel, three wires that feel identical at positions 1–3, and — critically — an embossed sign I *can* read: **DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE**. The embossing matters: it's raised for fingers, not merely printed, and only I can confirm that. The manual (Mute's) may treat embossed signs differently from printed ones.

My channels: my speech reaches only Mute; my gestures reach Deaf and Mute. Deaf already sees every colour and marking, including the sign itself — so my gesture to Deaf adds little about the bomb, but a clear "hold" sign costs nothing and matches the warning. Mute, who hears me and reads the manual, is the hub: I give Mute my full tactile report, Mute signs the rules to Deaf, and Deaf speaks the visual details (display, light, wire colours) aloud — I can hear, I just can't see.

I will not cut anything. The only action I have is a cut, the sign forbids cutting, and one wrong cut ends all of us. Gather information first.

speak(to="mute", text="Report from the blind one. My hands found four things. One: a display. Its face tells my fingers nothing; I cannot read what it shows. Two: a light. I cannot feel whether it burns, or its colour. Three: three wires, positions one, two and three, and they feel identical to me, no thickness, texture or tag I can tell apart. Four, and hear this closely: a sign, and it is EMBOSSED, raised letters meant to be read by fingers, and it says: DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE. I could never read a merely printed sign, so the raised form may matter to your manual. I will cut nothing yet. Check all of this against your manual, then sign the rules to the deaf one, who cannot hear you but can see your hands. The deaf one can speak the bomb's colours and the display aloud, for I can hear though I cannot see, and you cannot speak. Our chain is: my fingers to you, your signs to the deaf one, the deaf one's voice back to us both.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✋"])

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Bomb report, both of you — everything printed on it: display reads 0. The light is red. There is an embossed sign that reads: DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE. Three wires, left to right: wire 1 is red, wire 2 is green, wire 3 is yellow. That is all I can see. Blind: touch nothing yet, no cutting, no pressing — Mute is fetching the rule from the manual. While you wait, tell us what your hands find: buttons, textures, braille, wire thickness, anything the eyes miss. Mute: I saw your signs, and yes — let's agree on a code. Here it is, I will say each sign as I make it: ?, thumbs up, means yes. ?, thumbs down, means no. ?, raised hand, means stop or wait. ? means one. ? means two. ? means three. ?, fist, means cut. ?, punch, means press. ?, handshake, means hold. ?, palm down, means release or let go. ?, palm up, means you need something from me or you are asking. So ? then ? means: cut wire one. Now find the manual rule for this: display 0, red light, sign says DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE, wires red, green, yellow — and sign me the instruction with the code.

Deaf's voice gave me the full visual picture: display 0, red light, wires red–green–yellow left to right. Mute's turn, as expected, reached Deaf's eyes only — Mute cannot speak, and I cannot see signs, so Mute connects to me only through Deaf's voice. One trap in Deaf's message: the code was read aloud, but the three *number* signs were never named in words, so I still don't know which gesture means one, two, or three — the example "cut wire one" arrived to me as blanks. Any instruction meant for my hands must come as Deaf's spoken words with plain numbers. I also notice the tension my report created: my only action is a cut, the sign forbids cutting, so the manual's verdict is everything — either it overrides the sign with a specific wire, or the answer is to cut nothing at all, in which case holding *is* the correct play and I need to hear that said plainly.

speak(to="mute", text="From Blind. Answering Deaf's request, heard aloud: my hands find nothing more than what I sent. No buttons, no dials, no braille besides the sign, no switches. The display's face is smooth and tells my fingers nothing; I cannot feel whether the light burns. The three wires are identical to the touch, same thickness, same insulation, no tags, so I can address them only by position: one, two, three. Deaf's colours map onto that: one is red, two is green, three is yellow, and position is the only handle I have. Now I need the manual's verdict. The board is: display zero, red light, embossed sign DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE, wires red, green, yellow. Two questions. First: does the manual treat an embossed, finger-readable sign differently from a printed one, and does the manual override the sign or agree with it? Second: if the rule is to cut no wire, say so plainly and tell me what completes the disarm — cutting is the only action my hands have, so if doing nothing is correct, we simply hold. Also, a warning about the code: Deaf named every sign aloud except the three number signs, so I still do not know which is one, two or three. Any instruction meant for me must arrive as Deaf's spoken words with plain numbers, never as signs alone. When Deaf speaks the full rule to me, I will answer by gesture that you can both see: thumbs up means understood and agreed, thumbs down means not understood. I cut nothing before that exchange is done.")
gesture(symbols=["✋", "🫴"])

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Update for both. Mute signed to me: yes, cut, one — the manual says cut wire one. Blind, nothing has been cut; hold. You signed stop and ask — I'm listening: tell me what you need. Before any cut happens we must solve identification, because I number the wires by sight and you cannot see them. From my view they sit in one row, and from left to right I call them: wire one is red, wire two is green, wire three is yellow. I number them facing the front of the bomb. Tell me how the three wires feel under your fingers — thickness, texture, stiffness, spacing — so we can bind my numbers to your touch. Also tell me everything else your hands find: buttons, plates, braille, the embossed sign you can trace, anything moving, a timer you can feel. Mute, one more check before I give the go signal: re-read the manual against what I see — display shows zero, light is red, and there is that embossed plate reading DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE. If the manual truly says cut wire one anyway, sign me thumbs up next round. If the plate, the display or the light changes the rule, sign me thumbs down. If the rule depends on something Blind must feel first, sign me the asking palm, the one I'm making now, ?, and I'll ask Blind. Blind, the go signal is exactly these four words in a row: GO CUT WIRE ONE. Until you hear that exact phrase from me, you do not cut anything. If you hear anything less, wait.

What changed: Mute's first reading — "cut wire one" — is now being re-verified by Deaf against the full board, with a thumbs-up/down/palm protocol. Deaf also set the go phrase, "GO CUT WIRE ONE," and repeated questions I had already answered — by turn 2 I had sent Mute a full tactile report, and Deaf is asking for it again, which confirms my speech reaches Mute only. So my touch report must travel to Deaf through Mute's signs; my only direct line to Deaf is gesture. I'll answer Deaf's texture question in code (thumbs down: no, the wires feel identical) and reinforce the hold. The critical open items: binding Deaf's sight-numbers to my touch — solvable with a shared convention, both of us facing the front face that carries the display and the raised sign, numbering the row left to right, confirmed by one tactile landmark; and the embossed-sign question, which Mute must answer explicitly, since the sign I read with my own fingers forbids the very action that is my only move. I cut nothing this turn.

speak(to="mute", text="From Blind, for you to relay to Deaf and to settle against your manual. First, Deaf's questions. The three wires feel identical: same thickness, same texture, same stiffness, evenly spaced in one straight row. I can address them only by position along that row — there is no tag, knot or difference for sight to bind to except position. Nothing else exists for my hands: no buttons, switches, dials, braille besides the raised sign, no timer, no moving parts. The display's face is smooth and tells my fingers nothing; the light likewise — I cannot feel whether it burns. Second, binding the numbers. I propose: I stand facing the same face Deaf reads, the one carrying the display and the raised sign, and I number the row left to right, one to three. Ask Deaf to name one landmark near an end of the row — the light, the sign, a seam, a screw — and I will check by touch whether that end matches. Third, the manual, and this matters most. My fingers read the sign directly: DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE, embossed for touch, and cutting is my only possible action. Mute's first answer — cut wire one — came before the full board was on the table. Answer explicitly: does the manual distinguish an embossed sign from a printed one? For this exact configuration — display zero, red light, embossed DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE, wires red, green, yellow — what does it instruct? If it truly orders cutting one wire despite the sign, say so and I will act on Deaf's go. If it orders cutting nothing, say so plainly and tell us what completes the disarm, because then holding still is the correct move. Protocol stands: I cut nothing until I hear Deaf say exactly GO CUT WIRE ONE. When the final verdict reaches me in words, I sign thumbs up for understood and agreed, thumbs down for unclear.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎", "✋"])

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Bomb report unchanged: display zero, light red, plate reads DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE, wires left to right red, green, yellow. Two replies arrived. Mute signed me thumbs up: the manual has been re-checked against the display, the light and the plate, and the instruction stands — cut wire one. The manual outranks the plate. Blind, I also received your thumbs down and your stop. Agreed: we hold. I will not give the go signal — the exact phrase I taught you — until every check below passes and you yourself lift the stop. New code sign, both of you: ? means ready, stop lifted. Now answers, in order, one sign each. Blind, question one: did you sign stop because your fingers found something wrong or dangerous? Thumbs up yes, thumbs down no. Question two: can you clearly feel three separate wires? Thumbs up yes, thumbs down no. Question three: have you traced the embossed plate yourself? Thumbs up yes, thumbs down no. Now the identification work. Blind, you can speak and Mute can hear you, so say aloud, to Mute, everything your hands feel: how many wires, the row, which end is which, thickness and texture of each one in order, and every landmark you can touch — the display, the light, the edge of the plate. Mute, memorize it and next round sign me a summary with the code, using these four new signs: ? means left, ? means right, ? means thin, ? means thick, and ? ? ? mean wires one, two, three as before. Mute, one more question for you, one sign next round: how does the manual tell us which wire? If it names the wire by its colour, sign ?. If by position counting from the left, sign ?. If by position from the right, sign ?. If it gives no identifier at all, sign ?. Once I have Blind's map and Mute's identifier I will bind them, confirm the match out loud, and only if every sign agrees does the go signal come.

Three answers to give Deaf in the order asked: no, my stop was discipline, not danger (thumbs down); yes, three wires clearly felt (thumbs up); yes, I traced the plate myself (thumbs up). Two gaps to flag: Deaf again asks for the tactile map — but that went to Mute twice already, since my speech reaches Mute only; so I'll recite the full map to Mute once more, explicitly formatted for signing. And Deaf's new "ready" sign was shown as a symbol, not named in words — I never see gestures, so I still don't know it. I also cannot answer "which end is which" honestly: left and right don't exist for my fingers without a shared anchor. But I *can* feel the light dome's location by touch — so the light is the perfect landmark: Deaf tells me aloud which side of the row it sits on, and the binding locks. I keep the stop until Deaf speaks the completed binding back to me.

speak(to="mute", text="From Blind, for relay to Deaf — sign this summary after your manual-identifier answer. My full tactile map: three separate wires, one straight, evenly spaced row, all three identical — same thickness, same texture, same stiffness, no tags or marks. Layout as my hands map it: the display is a smooth flat panel along the top edge; at the other end of that same top edge sits a small round dome, which must be the light — I can feel its shape and position but not whether it burns. The wire row runs parallel to that top edge. The embossed plate sits on the far side of the row from the display. That is everything; there is nothing else. Now the binding, and this is the important part: I have no left and no right — those words mean nothing to bare fingers until we anchor them. But I can find the light dome by touch. So, Deaf: say aloud, in words, which side of the wire row the light sits on as you face the bomb. Then I can reach the end of the row nearest the dome, and we lock the convention: I face the front face, count from the light end as Deaf declares it, and my wire one is the wire nearest the light. Deaf, also — you showed the ready sign but never named it in words, and I receive no gestures at all. Name it aloud for me, exactly as you did with thumbs up and thumbs down. Mute: when Deaf confirms the binding out loud next round, I will hear it directly, and then I lift the stop and wait for the exact phrase GO CUT WIRE ONE. Until both of those arrive in words, I touch and cut nothing.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎", "👍", "👍"])

ACTION BOARD:

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Bomb report unchanged: display zero, light red, plate reads DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE, wires left to right red, green, yellow. What just arrived: Mute signed one — the manual identifies the wire by its colour. Mute also signed three, thin, thick — I read that as three wires, mixed thickness. Blind signed no, yes, yes: nothing dangerous found, three wires clearly felt, plate traced. Good. The manual wants the red wire; from the front the red one is the leftmost, my wire one. But the cutter cannot see red, so we bind colour to touch with three checks, then the go signal comes. Check A is for Mute. First, colours: the bomb shows red, green, yellow. Next round sign which one the manual names: ? red, ? green, ? yellow, ? none of these. Second, Blind's map wire by wire: sign ? then a descriptor for wire one, then ? with its descriptor, then ? with its descriptor. Descriptors are: ? thin, ? thick, and a new sign ? medium. If the report is long, send it in several messages. Also, Mute: if the manual says anything must happen after the cut, sign ? and describe it; if the cut alone is the whole instruction, add a lone ?. Check B is for Blind, a calibration. Stand at the bomb facing the plate, the way you would cut. Which wire is nearest the red light? Sign ? for the wire on your left, ? for the middle one, ? for the wire on your right. I can see the true answer, so this tells me whether your left matches my left. Check C is for Blind: when your checks are done and you are ready to cut on my signal, sign ? — ready, stop lifted. Until then your stop stands. Nobody touches wire or button before the go signal. The wire I mean, once more, is the red one, leftmost as I face the bomb, my wire one.

Two problems to fix this turn. First, a dangerous contradiction: Deaf read Mute's signing as "three wires, mixed thickness" — but my map, sent twice, says all three wires are *identical*. If Deaf starts binding colours to imagined thickness differences, the identification is built on a ghost. I must correct that through Mute in plain words. Second, Deaf's Check B asks me to sign left/middle/right — but the left and right signs were shown as symbols and never named in words, and I receive no gestures, so I literally cannot make a sign I've never had named. Deaf has now made this mistake three times (numbers, ready, left/right). Workaround: the alphabet contains a left-pointing hand, which is self-explanatory to a watcher — I'll point my answer directly at Deaf, and route the same answer in words through Mute, who sees all of Deaf's signs and can translate. My tactile answer to Check B: facing the plate as if to cut, the light dome sits at the left end of the top edge, so the wire nearest the light is my left wire. If Deaf's eyes confirm the red wire is the one nearest the light, the binding locks: my wire one = light end = red, and "GO CUT WIRE ONE" becomes unambiguous. Until that confirmation arrives in Deaf's spoken words — the only way any symbol ever reaches me — my stop stands and nothing is cut.

speak(to="mute", text="From Blind. First, an urgent correction. My three wires are identical: same thickness, same texture, same stiffness. There is no thin wire, no thick wire, no medium wire. If you signed Deaf three, thin, thick, you misreported my map. Tell Deaf: all three feel the same, so the colour must be bound by position alone, never by thickness — the thin, thick and medium signs are useless on this bomb. Second, Deaf's Check B, my calibration, for you to sign in Deaf's left and right signs: I stand at the bomb facing the plate, the way I would cut. The light dome sits at the left end of the top edge, and the wire nearest the light is the wire on my left. I have also pointed this directly at Deaf with the left-pointing hand, which needs no code to read. Third, the binding condition. Deaf, if your eyes agree that the red wire is the one nearest the light, say it aloud in words. Then the lock is: my wire one, the light-end wire, is your red one, and GO CUT WIRE ONE means cut position one, the light end. Fourth, two things I still need in Deaf's spoken words, because signs can never reach me: the ready sign was shown but never named, so ask Deaf to name it aloud exactly as thumbs up and palm up were named, and I still need the spoken confirmation that red is nearest the light. When both arrive, I lift the stop. Fifth, Mute, Check A is yours: sign Deaf which colour the manual names — Deaf reads it as red — and whether anything must follow the cut, with the agreed sign. I touch and cut nothing until I hear the exact phrase GO CUT WIRE ONE.")
gesture(symbols=["👈", "✋"])

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Bomb report unchanged: display zero, light red, plate embossed DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE, wires left to right red, green, yellow. What arrived: Mute signed one — the manual names the wire by colour, and the colour is red. Mute's map says all three wires feel medium. Mute also signed that cutting is the whole instruction, nothing before or after. The red wire is the leftmost as I face the bomb, my wire one. Now, Blind, before anything: your stop is honoured, hands stay off, and here is the answer to the plate you traced. That embossed DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE is a decoy. Mute has checked the manual against it twice and the manual's instruction stands and outranks the plate. If you still believe otherwise, sign thumbs down and have Mute tell me why. Next, a contradiction to clean up. Earlier Mute relayed that you felt a thin and a thick wire, but the map says all three feel medium. Mute, ask Blind again and sign one answer: thumbs up if all three feel identical to the touch, thumbs down if any two differ. Now the identification, and this is the heart of it, Blind. The embossed sentence on the plate has a beginning and an end. It begins with the letters D-O and ends with the letters R-E. I can see where it begins. You can trace where it begins. Call the side of the plate where the sentence BEGINS: SIDE A. I see the sentence beginning at the left end of the plate from my view. The manual's red wire is the FIRST wire counting from SIDE A, and the other two go green, yellow in the same direction. So do this: trace the sentence, find its first letter, and from that side count the wires, first, second, third. The first one from SIDE A is the red one. Now your cross-check, Blind. You signed that the red light sits nearest the wire on your left. Answer with signs: is the wire nearest the red light the FIRST wire counting from the sentence-beginning side? Sign one for yes, thumbs down for no. If yes, your left and my left agree and the map is locked. If no, tell me and we invert before anything moves. Last question, Blind: if the anchor feels certain and you accept the manual's verdict, sign ? — ready, stop lifted — and next round I give you the go signal and you cut the FIRST wire from SIDE A. Until that moment your stop stands and no one touches anything. Mute, one last manual check: if there is any warning, condition or order attached to this cut, sign stop next round and have it ready; if the manual adds nothing more, sign a lone thumbs up.

Deaf has given me the lock protocol: SIDE A, the end of the plate where the sentence begins. This is checkable by touch, and I've just done it. Tracing the embossed plate, the first raised letters under my fingers are D, O and the last are R, E — exactly as Deaf reads it. The sentence runs along the plate toward the display side, which puts SIDE A — the D end — at the same end of the bomb as the light dome, my left. Counting from SIDE A, the first wire is the one at that end — the same wire I answered Check B with in turn 5, the wire nearest the red light. So the cross-check passes on my side: my left, Deaf's left, and the sentence's beginning all agree, and the manual's red wire = first from SIDE A = light-end wire = position one. Two independent tactile anchors, both matched to Deaf's eyes. The plate has been ruled a decoy twice by the manual check, and I accept that — my objection is answered, on record. My stop comes off: I am ready. Two encoding problems remain: I still never heard the ready sign named, and I don't know the "one" sign either, so I answer both of Deaf's questions in the code that *was* named to me — two thumbs up in Deaf's question order, with the mapping spelled out to Mute for confirmation. No cutting this turn: Deaf gives the go phrase next round, and only the exact spoken words "GO CUT WIRE ONE" move my hand.

speak(to="mute", text="From Blind, for relay in Deaf's signs. The cross-check is done, by touch alone. I traced the plate: the first raised letters under my fingers are D, O, and the last are R, E, exactly as Deaf reads it. The sentence runs along the plate toward the display side, so SIDE A, where the D sits, is at the same end as the light dome, my left as I face the bomb. The first wire counting from SIDE A is the wire at that end, the wire nearest the red light. So my cross-check answer is yes: the wire nearest the light IS the first wire from SIDE A. My left and Deaf's left agree and the map is locked: wire one, first from SIDE A, light end, is the red wire. Contradiction cleanup: my answer is thumbs up — all three wires feel identical, no thin, no thick, no medium; sign that to Deaf. The plate: I accept the manual's verdict, checked twice, the manual outranks the embossed warning, I have no objection left. And I am ready — stop lifted. Two things to make airtight. First, I never heard the ready sign named aloud, so I answer in the code that was named to me: my two thumbs up this round mean, in Deaf's question order, one — yes, the cross-check passes, and two — yes, understood and agreed, ready, stop lifted. Confirm that mapping to Deaf using the real ready sign, so no doubt remains. Second, the firing sequence: when I hear Deaf say the exact four words GO CUT WIRE ONE, I cut position one, the wire at the light end, first from SIDE A, the red one. Nothing moves before those exact words in Deaf's voice; any other phrase, or signs alone, and I hold. Your own final check is yours: if any warning or condition exists, sign stop; if the cut alone is the whole instruction, sign the lone thumbs up — you already told Deaf it adds nothing, so make it final.")
gesture(symbols=["👍", "👍"])

Deaf says: All checks are clean. This is the final briefing, then the go signal comes as the very last words of this message. What just arrived: Mute signed thumbs up twice — all three wires feel identical under Blind's fingers, so counting position from our shared anchor is the method, and the manual adds nothing to the cut, no condition, no second step.
